transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. I came in because, well, the thought of getting on an airplane right now just scares me so bad. I know it doesn't really make sense, but... my body just tells me that the plane is going to fall.
Does this intense fear only happen when you think about or are near airplanes, or do you also feel this kind of fear in other situations that have nothing to do with flying?

No, it's really just the airplanes. I don't have this problem with anything else. I drive to work, I take the elevator, I don't mind heights or being in small spaces... it's just flying. If I'm not thinking about getting on a plane, I'm completely fine.

latest_inference.note: Fear is isolated to flying only, with no anxiety in other situations (heights, elevators, driving) and no general or panic-like symptoms reported, ruling out agoraphobia (F40.00), panic disorder (F41.0), and generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1). This is consistent with a specific (isolated) phobia of flying.
